body:
WGIUPD GENERAL INFORMATION SYSTEM DIVISION: Office of Health Insurance Programs 2/13/2026 PAGE 1 GIS 26 MA/05

The purpose of this General Information System (GIS) message is to inform local departments of social services (LDSS) of the revised federal poverty levels (FPLs). The revised FPLs are effective January 1, 2026, as published in the Federal Register.

The new FPLs should be used for all transactions with a Medicaid Budget Logic (MBL) eligibility “From” date of January 1, 2026, or later. The updated levels will be available in MBL on February 17, 2026. For all new and pending applications, income must be compared to the 2026 FPLs. All redeterminations effective January 1, 2026 or later, must be re-budgeted retroactive to January 1, 2026, using the Medically Needy Income Level (MNIL) based on the 2026 FPLs. As a result of the increase in the MNIL, the personal needs allowance amount for certain waiver participants and Managed Long Term Care enrollees who are subject to spousal impoverishment budgeting increases to $653 effective January 1, 2026.

Neither Phase 1 or Phase 2 of Mass Re-Budgeting (MRB), including the systematic update of the 2.8 percent (%) Cost of Living Adjustment (COLA) was run. Districts will be informed of any additional updates regarding MRB. Due to the increase in the FPLs, some Qualifying Individuals (QI) may be income eligible for the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) benefit. In such cases, staff must complete a 99-change transaction on the eMedNY Buy-in span, with the effective date of January 1, 2026, and change the Medicare Savings Program (MSP) code appropriately. For NYC, the change in MSP level can be transmitted via an undercare case transaction. Medicare Part B Premium In 2026, there is a COLA of 2.8% for Social Security benefits. Under a “hold-harmless” provision of federal law, a beneficiary’s Medicare Part B premiums in any year cannot rise higher than that year’s COLA. In 2026, most beneficiaries will pay the full Part B premium as the 2.8% COLA will generate enough increased income for them to pay $202.90 without reducing their net Social Security benefits. TO: Local District Commissioners, Medicaid Directors FROM: Gabrielle Armenia, Director Division of Eligibility and Marketplace Integration SUBJECT: 2026 Federal Poverty Levels ATTACHMENT: 2026 FPL Chart EFFECTIVE DATE: January 1, 2026 CONTACT PERSON: Local District Support Unit Rest of State (ROS) (518) 474-8887 NYC (212) 417-4500

WGIUPD GENERAL INFORMATION SYSTEM DIVISION: Office of Health Insurance Programs 2/13/2026 PAGE 2 GIS 26 MA/05

If an individual’s Social Security benefit does not increase enough for them to pay the $202.90 without their benefit decreasing, the “hold harmless” provision will limit the Part B premium increase to the amount of their 2026 Social Security benefit increase. The “hold-harmless” provision does not apply to all beneficiaries. The Medicare Part B premium for individuals in the following categories will increase to $202.90 (or higher) in 2026:

● Individuals whose income is above $109,000, or a married individual when the couple’s combined income is over $218,000, will pay the standard premium and an Income Related Monthly Adjustment Amount (IRMAA);

● New Medicare Part B beneficiaries since these individuals did not pay the Medicare Part B premium in 2025; and ● Individuals who do not have the Medicare Part B premium deducted from their Social Security benefit, including individuals who are enrolled in the Medicare Savings Program. These individuals will not be directly affected as the increased premium will be paid by Medicaid. If an individual has chosen to pay the Medicare Part B premium to reduce a spenddown obligation, the actual premium that is paid must be used in calculating the individual’s budget.

Family Member Allowance As a result of the increase in the FPLs, the amount used in the Family Member Allowance (FMA) formula increased to $2,705.00 and the maximum monthly FMA increased to $902. All spousal impoverishment cases involving a family member entitled to the family member allowance, with a budget effective date of January 1, 2026 or later and which were budgeted using the 2025 Family Member Allowance, must be re-budgeted using the 2026 Family Member Allowance. If a district determines that a previously budgeted case with a “From” date of January 1, 2026 or greater, has been negatively affected due to use of 2025 FPL, or if a case is brought to the district’s attention, the case should be re-budgeted using the revised FPLs. If eligible, covered medical expenses paid by an individual as a result of an improper calculation must be reimbursed pursuant to 10 OHIP/ADM-9, “Reimbursement of Paid Medical Expenses Under 18 NYCRR §360-7.5(a).” Congregate Care Medicaid eligibility for SSI-related consumers is determined by comparing income, after appropriate deductions, to the MNIL or the Medicaid Standard (and MBL Living Arrangement Chart as appropriate), and applying whichever income level is most beneficial. Special Income Standard for Housing Expenses

The special income standard for housing expenses that is available to certain individuals who enroll in the Managed Long-Term Care program (See 12 OHIP/ADM-5 and GIS 14 MA/017 for further information) varies by region. The 2026 amounts for each region have been updated based on the FPLs for 2026.

body: The following programs administered by Local Departments of Social Services, the Human Resources Administration in New York City, and the NY State of Health can assist individuals/couples in paying for their Medicare Premiums.
citation_label: Medicare Savings Programs 2026 (NYSDOH page, revised May 2026) 1
heading: Medicare Savings Program 2026

metadata.source_authority: New York State Department of Health, Office of Health Insurance Programs
metadata.title: Medicare Savings Programs 2026 (NYSDOH page, revised May 2026)

body:
This program pays for a wide range of medical care, services and supplies as well as premiums, coinsurance and deductible payments for Medicare beneficiaries. The 2026 income and resource requirements for those applicants are:

Income at or Below + $20 Resources at or Below Single: $1,836 per month $1,856 per month $33,038 Couple: $2,489 per month $2,509 per month $44,796

Note: Medicaid allows a $20 deduction from applicant’s gross monthly income when calculating eligibility for MSP. The income listed reflects the $20 monthly SSI general income disregard.
citation_label: Medicare Savings Programs 2026 (NYSDOH page, revised May 2026) 2
heading: Full Medicaid for Dual Eligibles (Individuals eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid)

metadata.source_authority: New York State Department of Health, Office of Health Insurance Programs

body:
This program can pay for the Medicare Part A and/or Part B premium. This program also pays for the Medicare Parts A and B coinsurance and deductibles. An individual can be eligible for QMB only or QMB and Medicaid The 2026 income requirements for this program are:

Income at or Below 138% FPL + $20 Single: $1,836 per month $1,856 Couple: $2,489 per month $2,509
citation_label: Medicare Savings Programs 2026 (NYSDOH page, revised May 2026) 3
heading: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary Program (QMB)

metadata.source_authority: New York State Department of Health, Office of Health Insurance Programs
metadata.title: Medicare Savings Programs 2026 (NYSDOH page, revised May 2026)

body:
This program pays for the Medicare Part B premium only. Individuals cannot be eligible for QI and Medicaid. The applicant must have Medicare Part A. States are allotted money for this program on a yearly basis. The 2026 income requirements for this program are:

Income Below 186% FPL +$20 Single: $2,474 per month $2,494 Couple: $3,355 per month $3,375

Applications for these programs may be obtained from the Medicaid office at the local (county) Department of Social Services. You may print the application from the link below or apply online with the NY State of Health. All paper applications for the Medicare Savings Program must be mailed to the local Department of Social Services where you live.

If you have questions, the phone number to call for the Medicaid Helpline is 1-800-541-2831.
